---
title: "The Quality-Control Report"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", out.width = "100%")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-images
#| include: false
figure_dir <- dirname(knitr::fig_path("report.png"))
dir.create(figure_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
cover_image <- file.path(figure_dir, "report-cover.png")
flagged_image <- file.path(figure_dir, "report-flagged.png")
figure_image <- file.path(figure_dir, "report-figure.png")
methods_image <- file.path(figure_dir, "report-methods.png")
pdf_cover_image <- file.path(figure_dir, "report-pdf-cover.png")
pdf_figure_image <- file.path(figure_dir, "report-pdf-figure.png")

shoot_section <- function(session, selector, path, first = selector) {
  bounds <- unlist(session$Runtime$evaluate(
    sprintf(
      "(function () {
        const top = document.querySelector('%s');
        const bottom = document.querySelector('%s');
        if (!top || !bottom) { return []; }
        return [
          top.getBoundingClientRect().top + window.scrollY,
          bottom.getBoundingClientRect().bottom + window.scrollY
        ];
      })()",
      first,
      selector
    ),
    returnByValue = TRUE
  )[["result"]][["value"]])
  if (length(bounds) != 2L) {
    stop(
      "The report has no element matching '",
      first,
      "' or '",
      selector,
      "'.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  shot <- session$Page$captureScreenshot(
    format = "png",
    captureBeyondViewport = TRUE,
    clip = list(
      x = 0,
      y = bounds[[1]],
      width = 1280,
      height = bounds[[2]] - bounds[[1]],
      scale = 1
    )
  )
  writeBin(jsonlite::base64_dec(shot[["data"]]), path)
}

make_report_images <- function() {
  brave <- "/Applications/Brave Browser.app/Contents/MacOS/Brave Browser"
  if (
    is.null(suppressMessages(chromote::find_chrome())) &&
      file.exists(brave) &&
      !nzchar(Sys.getenv("CHROMOTE_CHROME"))
  ) {
    Sys.setenv(CHROMOTE_CHROME = brave)
  }

  example <- NACHO::GSE74821
  limits <- example@thresholds
  limits[["FoV"]] <- 95
  example <- NACHO::normalise(example, outliers_thresholds = limits)

  report_dir <- tempfile("nacho-report-article-")
  on.exit(unlink(report_dir, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  html_report <- NACHO::render(
    example,
    format = "html",
    output_dir = report_dir,
    title = "PAM50 study, batch 3"
  )
  pdf_report <- NACHO::render(
    example,
    format = "typst",
    output_dir = report_dir,
    title = "PAM50 study, batch 3"
  )

  chrome_args <- chromote::default_chrome_args()
  if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("CI"))) {
    chrome_args <- c(chrome_args, "--no-sandbox")
  }
  chrome <- chromote::Chromote$new(
    browser = chromote::Chrome$new(args = chrome_args)
  )
  on.exit(chrome$close(), add = TRUE)
  browser <- chromote::ChromoteSession$new(
    parent = chrome,
    width = 1280,
    height = 900
  )
  browser$Page$navigate(paste0("file://", html_report))
  deadline <- Sys.time() + 60
  repeat {
    state <- browser$Runtime$evaluate("document.readyState")[["result"]][["value"]]
    if (identical(state, "complete")) {
      break
    }
    if (Sys.time() > deadline) {
      stop("The report did not finish loading within 60 seconds.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    Sys.sleep(0.2)
  }

  shoot_section(browser, "#title-block-header", cover_image)
  shoot_section(browser, "#decision-summary", flagged_image)
  shoot_section(browser, "#binding-density", figure_image)
  shoot_section(browser, "#methods", methods_image)

  pdf_pages <- pdftools::pdf_text(pdf_report)
  figure_page <- grep("Figure 1. Binding density", pdf_pages, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  for (job in list(
    list(page = 1, path = pdf_cover_image),
    list(page = figure_page, path = pdf_figure_image)
  )) {
    bitmap <- pdftools::pdf_render_page(
      pdf_report,
      page = job[["page"]],
      dpi = 100
    )
    png::writePNG(bitmap, job[["path"]])
  }
}

make_report_images()
```

The `render()` function writes the quality-control report of a `nacho` object.
The report is one file, either a self-contained HTML page or a tagged A4 PDF.
The HTML file needs nothing else to open, so you can email it or keep it with the data.
The PDF goes through Typst, which Quarto bundles, so you do not need LaTeX.
Both formats hold the same content, and this article shows a real report of the example data `GSE74821` in each.
The example raises the field-of-view limit to 95, so that one sample is flagged and the report has something to show.
The pictures come from a report that the website build renders each time.

## Create a report

Pass a `nacho` object to `render()`, and choose the format with `format`.
The call returns the path of the report, invisibly.

```{r}
#| label: render-call
#| eval: false
library(NACHO)

render(
  GSE74821,
  format = "html",
  output_dir = "reports",
  title = "PAM50 study, batch 3",
  author = "Jane Doe, Genomics Core"
)
```

The main arguments are these.

- `x` is the `nacho` object from `load_rcc()` or `normalise()`.
- `format` is `"html"` (the default) or `"typst"` for a PDF.
- `output_dir` is the folder that receives `nacho-report.html` or `nacho-report.pdf`.
  NACHO creates the folder when it does not exist.
- `title` replaces the default title, "NanoString quality-control report".
- `author` names who prepared the report, and shows on the cover when you give it.
- `group` is a column of `nacho_samples(x)` with the biological groups.
  With a group, the report also checks whether batches and groups are confounded.

Other arguments, such as `colour`, `size` and `outliers_labels`, change how the plots look.
`?render` lists all of them.
Rendering needs the Quarto command-line interface 1.9.18 or newer.

## Cover and decision summary

The report opens with a cover that gives the title, the date, the number of samples and cartridges, the number of flagged samples, the normalisation method, the RCC version and the NACHO version.
The decision summary follows.
It lists every flagged sample with the metrics that failed, and then adds notes on how the data were processed.
For example, a note tells you when the positive control model did not fit a sample.
Under the table, a "How to read this" box explains the columns.

```{r}
#| label: cover-html
#| echo: false
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   The cover of the HTML report on a dark banner. It shows the NACHO logo, the
#|   title "PAM50 study, batch 3", the preparation date and the cover details:
#|   48 samples, 4 cartridges, 1 flagged, GLM normalisation, RCC version 1.6 and
#|   the NACHO version.
knitr::include_graphics(cover_image)
```

```{r}
#| label: flagged-html
#| echo: false
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   The Decision summary section of the HTML report. Three tiles give the
#|   number of samples that pass, the number of flagged samples and the number of
#|   metrics behind the flags. A table lists the flagged sample with the metric
#|   that failed, and a "How to read this" box explains the table.
knitr::include_graphics(flagged_image)
```

## Settings and thresholds

A table lists each setting and limit that the report used.
Every row gives the value, what it means and where it comes from, for example the nCounter guidelines or a choice that you made.
A reader can tell which limits were the defaults and which were changed, without opening your code.

## Figures and tables

Each figure and each table has a "How to read this" box under it.
The box says what one point or one box stands for, which pattern is fine, and what to do when a pattern looks wrong.
The sections follow the quality-control metrics, the control probes, the counts, the principal components, the normalisation and the batch effects.

```{r}
#| label: figure-html
#| echo: false
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   The Binding density section of the HTML report. Text explains the metric
#|   and its limits, a box plot shows the binding density of the samples by
#|   cartridge with the limits as dashed lines in shaded bands, and a "How to read
#|   this" box under the plot explains the points, the boxes and the bands.
knitr::include_graphics(figure_image)
```

## Methods appendix

The report ends with a methods appendix.
It gives the citation of NACHO, a description of the methods that the data went through, and the versions of R and of the packages that made the report.
That makes the file a record that you can attach to a study, and that a colleague can reproduce.

```{r}
#| label: methods-html
#| echo: false
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   The Methods section of the HTML report. Paragraphs describe the limits
#|   and the normalisation, the versions of NACHO and R, and the reference to cite
#|   for NACHO. The session information starts below with the package versions.
knitr::include_graphics(methods_image)
```

## The PDF

The PDF has the same sections, laid out on A4 pages with a cover page, a table of contents and running headers.
It is tagged and declares PDF/UA-1, so screen readers can follow it.
Quarto may warn that verapdf is not installed.
The warning only means that Quarto skipped an extra validation step.

```{r}
#| label: cover-pdf
#| echo: false
#| out.width: "60%"
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   The cover page of the PDF report on a dark A4 page. It shows the NACHO logo,
#|   the title "PAM50 study, batch 3", the preparation date and the cover
#|   details: 48 samples, 4 cartridges, 1 flagged, GLM normalisation and the
#|   versions.
knitr::include_graphics(pdf_cover_image)
```

```{r}
#| label: figure-pdf
#| echo: false
#| out.width: "60%"
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A page of the PDF report with a running header. The binding density box plot
#|   sits at the top with its caption, followed by a "How to read this" box and the
#|   start of the Field of view section.
knitr::include_graphics(pdf_figure_image)
```
